title: Arcade Machines & Logic Circuits
description: The 1970s marked the birth of the commercial video game industry, transforming games from experimental laboratory projects into public entertainment. Early arcade systems used dedicated electronic circuits that directly controlled graphics and sound rather than relying on programmable processors.
caseStudy: Pong (1972): Every aspect of the game—including paddle movement, physics, and scoring—was implemented using hardwired electronic components like logic gates and flip-flops, without a CPU or RAM.

title: Home Consoles & 8-Bit Graphics
description: The 1980s marked a turning point as gaming shifted into homes. Home consoles became programmable systems using interchangeable ROM cartridges. The CPU processed game logic while specialized hardware handled graphics and sound.
caseStudy: Nintendo Entertainment System (NES): Powered by the Ricoh 2A03 8-bit processor, it separated computation from graphics by pairing the CPU with a dedicated Picture Processing Unit (PPU), establishing modern architectural divisions.

title: 16-Bit Processing & Early 3D Consoles
description: The 1990s pushed gaming into a new era through faster processors, improved graphics hardware, and significantly larger storage media. The architectural shift moved from flat 2D sprites to real-time 3D polygon rendering.
caseStudy: The Transition to Polygons: The PlayStation introduced the Geometry Transformation Engine (GTE) to accelerate geometric calculations, while the Nintendo 64 featured the Reality Co-Processor (RCP) for texture mapping and anti-aliasing.
games: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

title: Online Gaming & Sixth Generation
description: Gaming became highly connected. The rigid, fixed-function rendering pipelines of the 1990s gave way to highly flexible, programmable silicon. Consoles adopted architectures that mirrored personal computers, standardizing multi-platform development.
caseStudy: Halo 2 (2004): Engineered a robust networking layer directly atop the Xbox Live infrastructure. It automated lobby structures and utilized client-side prediction models with server-authoritative state checks to manage latency.

title: Mobile, Indie, & Streaming
description: The 2010s marked a crucial period of standardization. Hardware manufacturers consolidated around uniform x86-64 CPU instruction sets. Unified Memory Architectures (UMA) allowed CPUs and GPUs to share high-speed memory.
caseStudy: The Witcher 3 (2015): Abandoned static map loading for a complex spatial grid file hierarchy. Background threads fetched textures from mechanical drives based on player velocity, proving massive worlds could run without solid-state media.

title: Next Generation & Modern Frontiers
description: Traditional hardware bottlenecks have been completely re-engineered. Game engines leverage near-instantaneous file I/O operations, automated hardware-level ray calculations, and neural-network-driven resolution scaling.
caseStudy: Cyberpunk 2077: Utilizes Full Path Tracing and Nvidia DLSS. Ray data is routed into an AI neural network to denoise and generate frames, while NVMe Direct I/O streams gigabytes of high-resolution assets instantly.
